_comment: THE EDIT-RUN LOOP (#1020, "compile time is the new Hermes"). Down-only: `budgetSeconds` is a ceiling and may only fall. `cargo xtask measure --write` is its only writer and only ever lowers it — a gate run measures and reports but never writes, because a ratchet that records whatever the last run cost is a log. The numbers were RE-BASED ONCE, on 2026-09-12, under an owner ruling recorded as D-1020-B2 in docs/decisions.md: the wave-1 numbers were seeded from a workspace of one crate over clap and serde_json, and the workspace now holds nine crates over iroh, quinn, tokio, prost and rusqlite-bundled. An owner ruling is the only legitimate way a number in a down-only ledger rises, and these are down-only again from this baseline. Each entry states its measurement, the state of the tree it was measured on, and the headroom multiplier that produced the ceiling; a key whose measurement already sat under a third of its ceiling KEPT the ceiling and says so. `kotlinNativeLinkSeconds` is a null placeholder for wave 3 lane E. Keyed by hardware class, in the vocabulary of tests/journeys.json.

cleanCheckSeconds.headroom: RAISED 180 s -> 1200 s in the 2026-09-12 re-base: measured 541.7 s for `cargo check --workspace` from an empty `target/` at nine members, multiplier 2 rounded up to a round number (1083 -> 1200). The ruling's default multiplier is 3; it is tightened to 2 for the three large cold numbers in this file, because 3x of a number this size is a ceiling no plausible regression reaches — a budget nobody can miss is a log. The dependency graph is the expensive half and is already paid here (iroh, quinn, tokio, prost, rusqlite bundled, and `[profile.dev.package."*"] opt-level = 2`, which optimises every dependency once), so the six crates wave 2b adds cost far less than the first nine did. This is the number sccache and a warm CI cache exist to keep away from a developer at all; wave 1 measured 17.4 s for one crate.

incrementalCheckSeconds.headroom: KEPT at 10 s: measured 0.6 s for `cargo check --workspace` after one line appended to `crates/apps/tally/src/lib.rs` — an APP crate, which is the issue's wording and the case "one crate per app" protects, where wave 1 touched whichever member sorted first. 0.6 s is 6% of the ceiling, so the ceiling stands untouched. This is the number that decides whether v1 feels like v0, and the one number in this file whose meaning IS the promise: ten seconds is the point at which a developer stops running it and starts guessing, so if a measurement ever forces this one upward the answer owed is a structural fix — mold or lld for the link, sccache for the dependency half — and not a bigger number.

releaseBuildSeconds.headroom: RAISED 600 s -> 1000 s in the 2026-09-12 re-base: measured 240.3 s and 475.0 s for `cargo build --workspace --release` from an empty `target/release` on two runs at nine members — a 2x spread on one container, because a concurrent lane was building. Multiplier 2 on the higher sample (950 -> 1000), for the reason `cleanCheckSeconds` states and one more: the `pr` profile runs this step and scores it against this ceiling, so it is the one compile-time number a pull request goes red on, and a ceiling above `pr`'s own 1500 s budget could never fire. Wave 1 measured 28.9 s.

singleCrateTestSeconds.headroom: KEPT at 60 s: measured 2.4 s for `cargo test -p centraid-net` REPEATED — the heaviest crate in the workspace (iroh, quinn, tokio), and the steady state of the loop a red test puts you in, which is what this key names. 2.4 s is 4% of the ceiling. The number that is NOT this key, and is recorded here because it is the loop's real defect: alternating `cargo test -p centraid-net` with `cargo test --workspace` cost 185.8 s and 161.7 s on two measurements, against 2.4 s for either command repeated, because one package's feature resolution is not the workspace's union and the two invalidate each other's artifacts. That is a structural finding with a structural answer (one `cargo test` shape for both the gate and the iteration loop, or a `[workspace] default-members` that makes them the same graph), not a number to widen this ceiling with. Wave 1 measured 10.4 s for `cargo test -p xtask`, the cheapest crate.

coldLocalProfileSeconds.headroom: NEW in the 2026-09-12 re-base (D-1020-B2-1), and the reason the `local` budget could stay at 120 s. `cargo xtask gate --profile local` measured 1394.6 s with no debug artifacts on disk — clippy 587.6 s and `cargo test --workspace` 806.5 s, the SAME dependency graph compiled twice, once for clippy's check units and once for real artifacts to link 360 tests against. Multiplier 2 (2789 -> 3000), for the reason `cleanCheckSeconds` states. This ceiling exists so that a cold run cannot pass the warm feedback-time budget by being cold and cannot pass unscored either: `cargo xtask gate` detects whether every workspace member has a LINKED artifact in `target/debug/deps` (an `.rmeta` from a previous `cargo check` does not count, so a checked-only tree cannot buy a warm budget), charges a cold `local` run here, and FAILS a cold run for which this key states no ceiling. Only `local` has a cold ceiling: every other profile runs in CI on a runner that has never seen this workspace, so cold is its normal case and its `budgetSeconds` has to hold cold or it is not a budget.

kotlinNativeLinkSeconds.headroom: A PLACEHOLDER, and deliberately null (D-1020-B2-3). The issue's fourth compile-time number is the Kotlin/Native framework link time for the shared module, and nothing in this repository can link it yet — there is no Android SDK, no Xcode and no `mobile/` tree on this machine. Wave 3 lane E measures it on the hardware class it runs on and sets it, alongside the `mobile-jvm` profile in gate-budgets.json. A null cannot be ratcheted, so seeding it costs the down-only discipline nothing; what it buys is that the key is named before it is needed, so the lane that lands the module cannot land it without a number.
